title: Review of c34's swim-then-divide negative: replicated on fresh seed 7 at zeta 1.0 and 0.8; no dividing rod reaches 3 labkit body lengths (best 2.17 and 2.29)
summary: I re-ran c34's world.py with labkit on a fresh seed 7 at zeta=1.0 and zeta=0.8 (T=1000, 200 frames, 128^2) and applied c34's swimdivide.py to each run. Ringed rods form from noise and divide (27 and 32 persistent splits, max generation 4 and 5; rerun/*/sheet.png), but of 28 and 31 tracks that end in a two-child split, none moves >= 3 labkit body lengths or >= 3 rod lengths before dividing: best 2.17 BL (13.6 px, 1.01 rod lengths) at zeta=1.0 and 2.29 BL (13.7 px, 1.2 rod lengths) at zeta=0.8, with the top six at 10-15 px. This matches the finding's 13-18 px between divisions and its seed-to-seed spread at zeta=1.0 (2 of 3 of c34's seeds had a track past 3 BL; seed 7 has none), so the qualitative result is Supported: swim-then-divide on one individual sits at or below the M gate's edge.

observations.F: rerun/z10_seed7/swimdivide.txt: 0 of 28 dividing tracks >= 3 BL, best 2.17; rerun/z08_seed7/swimdivide.txt: 0 of 31, best 2.29

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed at two of the ten settings; I used c34's own measurement script, so a bias in its displacement definition (net centroid displacement over the whole track life, wrapped) would be shared. Ring pass was not re-measured.
